# @mono-agent/operator

Share one strict local operator protocol, discovery model, and renderer-neutral
conversation state between mono-agent operator products.

Operator surface.

## Responsibility

This library owns the versioned HTTP plus NDJSON contract between an
agent's selected operator channel and independent products such as terminal or
web renderers. It provides the only first-party wire decoder, trusted-loopback
client, owner-private discovery reader, deterministic conversation reducer,
available-action rules, and golden fixtures.

The wire identity is `mono-agent.operator.v1`, its discovery schema is
`mono-agent.operator-registry.v1`, and its routes live exclusively under `/v1`.
This is the single prerelease contract: there is no second generation to
negotiate, and any other version namespace fails closed before dispatch.

A model route is the atomic pair `{ runtime, id }`. The same model id reached
through two runtimes is two routes, so an override naming one half is never
resolved against the other half's default. Each route may also advertise an
exact `label`, the exact `efforts` it accepts, and its `contextWindow`; an
absent field means "not advertised" and is never guessed.

## Install / Usage

Existing registry artifacts under this package name belong to the predecessor
repository, not this v1 source. Do not install them during the source preview;
build this checkout through the
[workspace source setup](../../docs/getting-started/install.md) instead.

Build the library and its workspace dependencies:

```bash
pnpm --filter @mono-agent/operator... run build
```

Discover a running agent, connect, and reduce one turn without interpreting the
wire locally:

```ts
import {
  OperatorDirectory,
  createOperatorClientForEntry,
  discoverOperators,
  initialOperatorState,
  reduceOperatorFrame,
} from "@mono-agent/operator";

const directory = new OperatorDirectory(await discoverOperators());
const entry = directory.select("personal-agent");
const client = createOperatorClientForEntry(entry);
let state = initialOperatorState("operator:example");

for await (const frame of client.streamTurn({
  conversationId: state.conversationId,
  input: { text: "Summarize the current project." },
})) {
  state = reduceOperatorFrame(state, frame);
}
```

Discovery descriptors contain only the environment variable name for an
optional bearer token. The secret itself is resolved when the client is
constructed and is never returned as directory state.

## Architecture

### Data flow

1. The owning state/discovery lifecycle publishes an owner-private descriptor
   containing the literal loopback endpoint; `channel-operator` serves that
   endpoint and does not own registry persistence.
2. A product discovers and selects a registry entry, then `OperatorClient`
   validates the endpoint, rejects redirects, submits bounded JSON to `/v1`,
   and decodes bounded NDJSON.
3. Every turn starts with `accepted`, carries only validated frames, and ends
   with exactly one `completed` or `error`; stopping iteration aborts the request.
4. The reducer retains bounded structured status, tool-call, tool-result, and
   compaction activity for product-owned replay while thought deltas exist only
   during the active turn. Usage snapshots retain the latest numeric counters
   while compaction and provider-session-eviction flags stay sticky.
5. Inline attachment URLs and quote text use shared hard bounds; the serving
   channel remains responsible for decoding attachments and verifying quote
   identities against authoritative conversation replay. Message identities are
   opaque: legacy-safe ids retain their spelling, while broader canonical Core
   ids use one deterministic bounded wire encoding.
6. Conversation summaries carry an explicit `cron` or `webhook` trigger kind
   only for externally delivered proactive conversations; products never infer
   provenance from an opaque conversation id or import Core's internal trigger
   execution thread.
7. Products pass decoded frames to `reduceOperatorFrame` and render the returned
   state and `availableOperatorActions` without a second decoder or reducer.

| Source module | Responsibility |

| [`types.ts`](https://github.com/robertsreberski/mono-agent-next/blob/main/packages/operator/src/types.ts) | Versioned protocol, request, response, frame, directory, and view contracts. |
| [`protocol.ts`](https://github.com/robertsreberski/mono-agent-next/blob/main/packages/operator/src/protocol.ts) | Strict parsers and bounded server-side frame serialization. |
| [`client.ts`](https://github.com/robertsreberski/mono-agent-next/blob/main/packages/operator/src/client.ts) | Redirect-rejecting loopback HTTP client and terminal-enforcing NDJSON decoder. |
| [`directory.ts`](https://github.com/robertsreberski/mono-agent-next/blob/main/packages/operator/src/directory.ts) | Owner-private registry reads, deterministic normalization, selection, and token resolution. |
| [`state.ts`](https://github.com/robertsreberski/mono-agent-next/blob/main/packages/operator/src/state.ts) | Deterministic conversation reducer and shared action eligibility. |
| [`testing.ts`](https://github.com/robertsreberski/mono-agent-next/blob/main/packages/operator/src/testing.ts) | Golden valid, malformed, AskUser, and reducer fixtures under `./testing`. |

## Public API

### Start here

| API | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `OperatorClient` | Submit turns and consume strict decoded frames over a trusted loopback endpoint. |
| `discoverOperators` / `OperatorDirectory` | Read owner-private registries and select or pin an agent deterministically. |
| `initialOperatorState` / `reduceOperatorFrame` | Produce the same renderer-neutral state in every product. |
| `availableOperatorActions` | Gate cancel, live input, AskUser, overrides, attachments, quoting, and views from one policy. |
| `evaluateOperatorRuntimeOverride` | Apply one deterministic capability/model/effort eligibility decision in every renderer before Core validation. |
| `assertOperatorIdentity` | Bind endpoint info to the selected registry agent id, process id, and process start time before use. |
| `parseOperatorFrame` / `serializeOperatorFrame` | Implement a compliant server without duplicating bounded thought, activity, tool, compaction, or terminal-frame validation. |
| `OPERATOR_ROUTES` / `OPERATOR_LIMITS` | Share route names and hard protocol bounds with servers and tests. |
| `@mono-agent/operator/testing` | Reuse golden streams to prove product parity. |

## Dependency Boundary

The package has no production dependency on core, a runtime, a channel,
persistence, a renderer, or an HTTP framework. It uses only Node.js APIs and
web-standard fetch/stream primitives. Agent channels may depend on this package
for protocol contracts; standalone products depend on it for client and domain
behavior.

## What This Package Does Not Own

It does not bind an HTTP server, dispatch agent turns, persist web or terminal
product state, render widgets, upload files, send notifications, configure an
agent, manage services, expose a public-network endpoint, or stop an agent when
a renderer exits. It does not define a generic product or plugin registry.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm --filter @mono-agent/operator run build
pnpm --filter @mono-agent/operator run typecheck
pnpm --filter @mono-agent/operator run test
```

Focused tests cover valid, malformed, oversized, incomplete, delayed, and
consumer-disconnected streams; owner/mode/symlink registry rejection; endpoint
and redirect policy; the module-sdk-aligned AskUser byte/shape contract;
reducer determinism; and action parity.
